title: Lowpoly Arbitrary N-Gon Faces And Coplanar Merge
description: Support arbitrary vertex/edge count faces (n-gons) in the lowpoly mesh kernel end to end: Newell-method face normals (robust for non-planar/collinear-first-corner n-gons), ear-clipping triangulation replacing the convex-only fan (tessellate, triangulate command, UV unwrap), and a real merge_coplanar_faces + dissolve_edges implementation (currently a no-op stub) with a collinear-vertex cleanup pass. Regenerate the "Concrete Forest Left" default example mesh with all coplanar faces merged into n-gons instead of the current all-triangle tessellated output.
summary:
Added full arbitrary n-gon support to the lowpoly mesh kernel (kernel/3d/mesh/rs/lib.rs) and regenerated the "Concrete Forest Left" default example with coplanar faces merged.

1. **Newell-method face normals**: `face_normal` now uses Newell's method over the full loop (computed in f64) instead of the first-triangle cross product, which degenerated to a zero vector whenever a face's first corner was collinear with its neighbors — guaranteed on merged n-gon boundaries.
2. **Ear-clipping triangulation**: new `triangulate_polygon` helper (Newell normal → least-parallel-axis projection basis → deterministic ear clipping in f64, with an automatic fan fallback on degenerate input) replaces the old convex-only fan in `tessellate()`, the `triangulate()` command, and the LSCM UV-unwrap system (`solve_island_uv`). Concave n-gons now tessellate, triangulate, and unwrap correctly.
3. **`merge_coplanar_faces()`** (new op) + **`dissolve_edges()`** (previously a no-op stub) now share a real pairwise face-loop merge core (`merge_face_loops`): splices two adjacent face loops across their one shared edge, rejecting results that would produce a repeated vertex (non-simple/holed polygon). `merge_coplanar_faces` greedily merges every adjacent face pair whose Newell normals are parallel and whose union is planar within kernel tolerances, then runs a `collinear_cleanup` pass that drops vertices which are a straight ~180° pass-through in *every* face loop that references them — turning triangulated slabs into clean n-gons instead of leaving chains of collinear seam vertices.
4. Fixed two broken test attributes (a doubled `#[test]` and a test missing its `#[test]` entirely, so it never ran).
5. Added 6 new kernel tests: Newell normal on a collinear-first-corner quad, ear-clipping area/winding correctness on a concave L-hexagon, `merge_coplanar_faces` reassembling a triangulated cube back into 6 quads, `dissolve_edges` merging two triangles into a quad, merge+cleanup collapsing seam vertices of a 3-quad strip into one clean quad, and concave-face tessellation tagging all triangles with one face id.
6. `lowpoly/core/rs/tests/export_concrete_forest_mesh.rs`: added a `merge_coplanar_faces()` call (with assertions that face count drops and at least one merged face has >4 corners) between BREP tessellation and UV unwrap. Regenerated `lowpoly/example/concrete-forest-left.mesh.json` and `lowpoly/example/default.lowpoly.json` via a script in this ticket folder — face count dropped from 109 (all triangles) to 57 (33 quads, 17 triangles, 2 pentagons, 5 hexagons), halfedges 327→223, vertices unchanged at 70.

Verification: `cargo test -p kernel_3d_mesh` 19/19 passing (including the 2 previously-dead tests and 6 new ones). `cargo test -p lowpoly_core` 13/13 + 3/3 integration tests passing against the newly-embedded merged example. Rebuilt the lowpoly plugin wasm via the real dev pipeline and confirmed live in the browser: the Document panel correctly shows the reduced face/edge counts (Faces 57, Edges 111, Vertices 70) and the merged n-gon mesh renders visually identically to before (no missing/flipped triangles from the concave merged faces), confirming the ear-clipping triangulation works correctly end to end.
